description:
Code and supporting results of the paper 'Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling', which introduces MAD-COSMO, a collection of about 1.7 billion structures from public atomistic datasets, and MAD-CORE, its nested coreset of 2^24 structures selected by farthest point sampling and accretion in the space of the ecumetric, a learned structural descriptor.

What can be reproduced from this deposit. The source archive regenerates Figures 1 and 3 to 10 of the paper and the three figures of the supporting information from the numerical inputs it contains (verified pixel for pixel against the submitted files), regenerates the four tables of the supporting information from their source files, and holds the scripts and committed outputs behind every number stated in the text, two of which were rerun against the released data for this deposit. The supporting-results archive holds the per-structure predictions, feature-reconstruction descriptors and Voronoi populations from which those numerical inputs are recomputed. The models archive holds the thirteen trained PET checkpoints (trained from scratch, fine-tuned, learned r2SCAN-LDA and r2SCAN-PBE corrections, direct r2SCAN fine-tune) evaluated in the paper.

What is provided as an upstream workflow only. The data collection and covalent-radius prefilter, the training of the ecumetric model, the featurisation of the collection, the farthest point sampling and accretion runs, the Voronoi tessellation, the sketch-map fit, the DFT labelling campaign, the model trainings and the molecular dynamics are included as the code, configurations, manifests and run records that produced the results, with their resource requirements; they were not rerun for this deposit and need multi-GPU or multi-node resources, the FHI-aims code and the project's data store.

Limitations. Figure 2 is a hand-drawn illustration. Two columns of the supporting-information table of accretion levels (margin and time) come from a run log that was deleted and cannot be regenerated. The structure counts of the LDA and PBE label files in the MAD-CORE record are 79,220 and 77,362 against 79,241 and 77,383 printed in Table I. The collection was prefiltered with a covalent-radius contact criterion before the ZBL filter described in the paper. The torch sketch-map implementation used for the fit of Figure 8 is in an uncommitted fork of scikit-matter. The data-collection code is unversioned and is included as a snapshot with file hashes. The structures, features and DFT labels themselves are in the MAD-CORE and MAD-COSMO records on the Materials Cloud Archive, not in this deposit.
